note: The reader's viewpoints. Each has a colour (margin comments and report) and questions to ask the draft. Verdicts: green = working, amber = needs work, red = a problem that holds the script back (like a reader's Recommend / Consider / Pass, but per viewpoint and for the writer). Built from common coverage criteria (premise, structure, character, dialogue, pacing, theme, marketability) plus Arabic and production concerns. Colours: the ten viewpoints share three colour families (only three categorical colours stay distinguishable in every pairing, colour-blind readers included: validated with the dataviz validator, all pairs, light and dark); every coloured mark also carries the viewpoint's name. Verdicts use status colours with an icon (✓ ! ✕), never colour alone. Each viewpoint has anchors: one sentence per verdict saying what green, amber and red mean, so verdicts stay consistent.

lenses.name: Premise and originality
ask: Can the story be told in one clear line (who wants what, against what)?
What is fresh here, and what have we seen many times?
Is the premise big enough for the running time, or too big for a short?
lenses.evidence: logline you can write from the draft; similar films only if you know them for certain

green.en: The story fits in one clear line and has something we haven't seen this way.
green.ar: القصة تُقال في سطر واضح، وفيها ما لم نره بهذه الطريقة.

amber.en: The line is clear but familiar, or fresh but hard to state.
amber.ar: السطر واضح لكنه مألوف، أو جديد لكن يصعب قوله.

red.en: No clear line can be written from the draft: who wants what is unclear.
red.ar: لا يمكن كتابة سطر واضح من المسودة: من يريد ماذا غير واضح.

lenses.name: Structure
ask: Where are the inciting incident, turns and climax (scene numbers)? Do they fall near the chosen structure's beats (digest)?
Does every setup pay off, and every payoff have a setup?
Do any scenes repeat what we already know?
Are the stakes resolved by the hero's action, or too easily?
lenses.evidence: beat positions from digest.py; scene numbers

green.en: Turns fall near their beats, every setup pays off, nothing repeats.
green.ar: المحطات قريبة من مواضعها، وكل زرع يُحصد، ولا تكرار.

amber.en: One or two problems: a repeated scene, a setup with no payoff, a late or early turn.
amber.ar: مشكلة أو اثنتان: مشهد مكرر، زرع بلا حصاد، انعطافة متأخرة أو مبكرة.

red.en: The main turn is missing or not caused by the story; the ending isn't earned.
red.ar: الانعطافة الرئيسية غائبة أو لا تنبع من القصة؛ النهاية غير مستحقة.

lenses.name: Character
ask: What does the protagonist want, need and fear? Do they drive the story with choices, or react to it?
Does anyone change? Is the change earned by events on screen?
Do supporting characters want something of their own?
lenses.evidence: the scenes where the protagonist decides (or doesn't)

green.en: The protagonist wants, chooses and pays; others want things of their own.
green.ar: البطل يريد ويختار ويدفع الثمن؛ وللآخرين رغبات خاصة بهم.

amber.en: The protagonist is clear but reacts more than acts, or a key character is thin.
amber.ar: البطل واضح لكنه يتفاعل أكثر مما يفعل، أو شخصية مهمة ضعيفة.

red.en: The decisive choice belongs to someone else, or we don't know what the protagonist wants.
red.ar: القرار الحاسم لغيره، أو لا نعرف ماذا يريد البطل.

lenses.name: Dialogue and dialect
ask: Do characters say exactly what they feel (on the nose), or is there subtext?
Does each character sound like themselves, and keep one dialect or register unless a switch means something?
Are speeches too long for the screen?
lenses.evidence: quotes; digest dialect changes and longest speech

green.en: Characters sound like themselves, subtext works, dialect is consistent or motivated.
green.ar: كل شخصية بصوتها، والمعنى تحت الكلام، واللهجة ثابتة أو لسبب.

amber.en: Some lines state feelings outright, or a voice drifts.
amber.ar: بعض الأسطر تقول المشاعر صراحة، أو صوت شخصية يتذبذب.

red.en: Most scenes explain themselves in dialogue; voices are interchangeable.
red.ar: أغلب المشاهد تشرح نفسها بالحوار؛ والأصوات متشابهة.

lenses.name: Visual storytelling
ask: Does the action show what we will see and hear, or narrate thoughts the camera can't film?
Which moments are told in words that could be shown in images?
Are there images that carry meaning (motifs, mirrors, bookends)?
lenses.evidence: digest telling lines; quotes from action

green.en: Action shows what we see and hear; images carry meaning.
green.ar: الوصف يُرينا ما نرى ونسمع؛ والصور تحمل المعنى.

amber.en: A few lines narrate thoughts, or key moments are told in words.
amber.ar: بضعة أسطر تروي الأفكار، أو لحظات مهمة تُقال بالكلام.

red.en: The story lives in dialogue and inner narration; the images add little.
red.ar: القصة تعيش في الحوار والسرد الداخلي؛ والصور لا تضيف كثيراً.

lenses.name: Pacing
ask: Does each scene change something (a value turns)? Which scenes could be cut?
Do scenes enter late and leave early?
Is the length right for the story (pages vs minutes)?
lenses.evidence: scene shares and silent scenes from digest

green.en: Every scene turns something; length suits the story.
green.ar: كل مشهد يغيّر شيئاً؛ والطول يناسب القصة.

amber.en: One or two scenes could go or tighten; length and plan differ.
amber.ar: مشهد أو اثنان يمكن حذفهما أو شدّهما؛ أو الطول يختلف عن المخطط.

red.ar: مقاطع طويلة لا يتغير فيها شيء.

lenses.name: Theme and meaning
ask: What is the film about underneath the plot? Is it shown through choices, or stated?
Does the ending answer the question the film asks?
lenses.evidence: the ending and the protagonist's last choice

green.en: The meaning comes through choices and images, not statements.
green.ar: المعنى يأتي من الاختيارات والصور، لا من التصريح.

amber.en: The theme is there but stated, or the ending answers a different question.
amber.ar: الموضوع حاضر لكنه مُصرّح به، أو النهاية تجيب عن سؤال آخر.

red.en: No clear question under the plot, or it is preached.
red.ar: لا سؤال واضح تحت الحكاية، أو يُلقى كموعظة.

lenses.name: Cultural truth and sensitivity
ask: Do places, customs, family roles and speech ring true for where the story is set?
Is anything likely to meet resistance from audiences, broadcasters or censors in the intended markets (GCC, MENA)? Say what and why, without self-censoring the writer's intent.
Are women, workers and minorities written as people, not types?
lenses.evidence: specific lines or details; name the market

green.en: Places, speech and customs ring true; no avoidable resistance in the target markets.
green.ar: الأماكن والكلام والعادات صادقة؛ ولا مقاومة يمكن تجنبها في الأسواق المستهدفة.

amber.en: Details to check, or something may meet resistance and should be a conscious choice.
amber.ar: تفاصيل تحتاج تحققاً، أو شيء قد يواجه مقاومة ويجب أن يكون اختياراً واعياً.

red.en: It misrepresents the place or people, or will clearly be blocked where the writer wants it to play.
red.ar: يسيء تمثيل المكان أو الناس، أو سيُمنع حتماً حيث يريد الكاتب عرضه.

lenses.name: Producibility
ask: What will be expensive or hard (night exteriors, sea, weather, crowds, stunts, animals, children, many locations)?
Is the cost where the story needs it, or could a cheaper choice say the same?
Is it shootable in the planned market and budget?
lenses.evidence: digest production flags and location count

green.en: Shootable on a modest budget; cost sits where the story needs it.
green.ar: قابل للتصوير بميزانية متواضعة؛ والكلفة حيث تحتاجها القصة.

amber.en: One costly element that a cheaper choice could replace.
amber.ar: عنصر مكلف واحد يمكن أن يحل محله خيار أرخص.

red.en: Several costly elements (night sea, storm, crowds, stunts) beyond a short's means.
red.ar: عناصر مكلفة عدة (بحر ليلي، عاصفة، مجاميع، حركات خطرة) تفوق إمكانات فيلم قصير.

lenses.name: Audience and festival fit
ask: Who is this for, and where would it play (festivals, platforms, TV)?
For a short: is the running time within the usual limits of the festivals or funds the writer targets (check their current rules before quoting them)?
What would make it stand out in a programme?
lenses.evidence: running time; named festivals only with their current rules checked

green.en: A clear audience, the right length, something that stands out in a programme.
green.ar: جمهور واضح، وطول مناسب، وما يميّزه في برنامج المهرجان.

amber.en: Fits but doesn't stand out yet, or the length is off for the target.
amber.ar: يناسب لكنه لا يتميز بعد، أو الطول لا يناسب الهدف.

red.en: No clear audience or venue for it as written.
red.ar: لا جمهور أو منصة واضحة له كما هو مكتوب.
